page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i2g.16xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8163 processors. It features 64 virtual CPUs, corresponding to 32 physical cores with hyper-threading, operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB per core. A key hardware feature is the inclusion of 7679 GB of bundled local SSD storage, alongside a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps. The instance runs on the KVM hypervisor and supports AVX and AVX512F instruction sets.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance tradeoff characterized by moderate multi-threaded capabilities and weak single-core performance. Single-core metrics, such as Geekbench single-core and stress-ng single-core CPU tests, fall into the bottom 25% tier, while single-threaded gzip compression registers in the bottom 10%. Conversely, multi-threaded execution is significantly stronger, with bzip3 multi-threaded decompression scoring in the top 25% at 199.24 GB/sec. General multi-core benchmarks, including Geekbench multi-core, Passmark CPU, and software compilation, consistently align with the middle 50% average tier.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.i2g.16xlarge offers high resource density due to its massive bundled local SSD storage. This makes it a viable option for workloads that require large local scratch space or high-capacity database storage without relying on external block storage. Given the balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and average multi-core performance, this instance is suited for database hosting, static web serving, and general-purpose enterprise applications that can leverage parallel processing to offset the lower single-core execution speeds.
